open_questions.detail: The type ramp uses 'Fraunces' (display serif) and 'Geist' (body sans) throughout. Fraunces is a standard Google Fonts family; Geist is Vercel's typeface and is not reliably available on the classic Google Fonts CDN — it needs self-hosting (e.g. the `geist` npm package or Fontsource) or a fallback stack.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed the implementer will self-host Geist (npm package / Fontsource) with a system-sans fallback, and load Fraunces from Google Fonts as normal.

open_questions.detail: The hero eyebrow pill ('AUTHENTIC NEAPOLITAN WOODFIRED', node 6:27) uses a vector literally named 'fire-extinguisher' (node 6:679), and the rendered PNG confirms it draws an extinguisher, not a flame — a surprising icon choice to pair with a wood-fired claim.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Ship the Icon exactly as drawn (name='fire-extinguisher') since the PNG is authoritative for visuals; did not silently substitute a flame icon.

options.label: Keep the fire-extinguisher glyph — matches node 6:679 and the rendered PNG exactly
Swap to a flame/fire icon — better matches the 'woodfired' copy, likely the original intent

open_questions.topic: Two cart entry points in the header
open_questions.detail: The header has both a text NavLink labelled 'Cart' (node 6:18) and a separate icon+badge CartButton (node 6:22, badge count '3'). Nothing in the frame distinguishes their destinations.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed both link to the same cart route/drawer and built them as independent components (NavLink and CartButton) that happen to share a destination, rather than merging them into one control.

open_questions.topic: Inconsistent alignment inside the second delivery-banner stat
open_questions.detail: In the 'Pizza Temperature' StatItem (node 6:51), the label (6:52) is right-aligned flush to the block's right edge, but the value line below it (6:53, 'Piping Hot Guaranteed') spans the full block width and is left-aligned — the label and value don't share one text-align.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Modelled StatItem with a single `align` prop applied to the label only, and left-aligned the value as drawn, since that is what the absolute positions show.

open_questions.topic: Card 4 (Prosciutto) is internally taller than its siblings
open_questions.detail: PizzaCard node 6:96's content block (6:97) is 377px tall vs. 356px for the other three cards (6:61, 6:73, 6:85), because its description text (6:103) wraps to one extra line. All four outer card frames are still 441px, implying the Figma auto-layout absorbs the difference as extra internal gap rather than growing the card.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed this is unintentional copy-length drift rather than a deliberate variant, and built one PizzaCard component with a fixed-height description area (line-clamped or min-height) so all four cards render at a uniform height in code, rather than reproducing the uneven internal gap pixel-for-pixel.
